headline: Admins invite people to a workspace by e-mail, and the invite stops working after seven days
lead: Today an admin creates the account and sends the password by hand. From now on they type an e-mail, the person gets a link, sets their own password and lands in the workspace.
problem: Accounts are created by hand and passwords travel over chat.
solution: An invite link, valid for seven days, that the person opens to set a password.
how: The admin types an e-mail; the system sends a link; the person opens it, sets a password and is in. After seven days the link shows as expired and the admin can send a new one.

external.q: What if the e-mail is already a member?
external.a: The admin sees it on the spot and nothing is sent.
Yes: the admin removes it from the pending list and the link stops working.

internal.a: E-mail delivery: a link that never arrives looks like a broken invite.

notBuilding.why: future direction; one at a time is enough for the first customers
every invited person is a member; roles are set later

bets.claim: The e-mail provider delivers within a minute
Seven days is enough for people to open the link
